subject: ss-neurology
title: Disease-modifying therapy in multiple sclerosis: choosing and monitoring treatment

steps.tx: Multiple sclerosis is an immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the CNS. Diagnosis needs **dissemination in time** and **dissemination in space**, as per the McDonald criteria. First-degree relatives carry a risk of about 2 to 4 percent, far above the general population. Disease-modifying therapy aims to reduce relapses and slow disability by dampening the CD4 positive proinflammatory T cell attack within the CNS.
steps.say: Multiple sclerosis is an immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system. Diagnosis needs dissemination in time and dissemination in space, as per the McDonald criteria. First-degree relatives carry a risk of about 2 to 4 percent, far above the general population. Disease-modifying therapy aims to reduce relapses and slow disability by dampening the CD4 positive proinflammatory T cell attack within the CNS.

steps.tx: Choose therapy according to **disease activity**. **Interferon beta** and **glatiramer acetate** are first-line, moderate efficacy agents, and **teriflunomide** also sits in this group. Glatiramer 40 mg three times weekly reduces enhancing lesions more than the 20 mg daily dose, so the higher schedule is an option for some patients. Highly active disease usually prompts escalation to stronger agents, weighing **infection risk** and the monitoring burden of each drug.

steps.tx: **Natalizumab** blocks leukocyte adhesion and migration into the CNS, but carries a risk of **progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy** linked to JC virus. Test anti-JC virus antibodies before starting. **Alemtuzumab** depletes CD52 positive cells and causes later secondary autoimmunity, mainly thyroid disease, so thyroid and blood tests continue for 48 months after the last dose.
steps.say: Natalizumab blocks leukocyte adhesion and migration into the central nervous system, but carries a risk of progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy linked to JC virus. Test anti-JC virus antibodies before starting. Alemtuzumab depletes CD52 positive cells and causes later secondary autoimmunity, mainly thyroid disease, so thyroid and blood tests continue for 48 months after the last dose.

steps.tx: **Fingolimod** is a sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator that keeps lymphocytes within lymph nodes, reducing their passage into the central nervous system. Before the first dose, obtain a baseline **ECG** and observe the patient for **bradycardia**, as heart rate can fall after starting. Stopping it abruptly may cause **rebound disease**, so plan a bridging disease-modifying therapy. **Cladribine** is a purine analogue given as short oral courses; screen for active infection and malignancy, and avoid it in pregnancy.

steps.tx: Pregnancy planning changes choice. **Teriflunomide** is teratogenic and persists for long because of enterohepatic recirculation; stop it before conception and use accelerated elimination with cholestyramine, confirming low levels. Glatiramer is widely regarded as safe during breastfeeding. The AAN advises against starting DMTs in pregnancy unless disease activity is high. Avoid live vaccines during immunomodulating therapy and defer vaccines during an active relapse.

steps.tx: Manage acute relapses with **methylprednisolone** 1 gram intravenously daily for 5 days. If there is no response, **plasma exchange** is the next step, given as 3 to 7 sessions daily or every other day. Symptoms such as the Lhermitte sign and constipation are managed with patient education, fibre and bulk-forming agents, and phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors for erectile dysfunction.
